evidence: deepseek uses "hopcroft_karp" on "left and right partitions" to obtain a maximum independent set, while the other solutions explicitly say "pick the larger color class" and then select enough vertices
affordance_in_statement: A subset is considered safe if it contains absolutely no interference links between any of its members. Given a required subset size k, determine if a safe subset of exactly k components can be formed. If it can, output one such valid subset.
secondary_shortcut_name: infer bipartiteness from the voltage condition
removal_suggestion: Require the output subset to be inclusion-wise maximal as well as safe: every component outside the subset must share an interference link with at least one selected component. This prevents simply taking an arbitrary k-element truncation of a larger independent set.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the voltage guarantee to treat the graph as bipartite, computes a maximum independent set with bipartite matching, and can then truncate it to k vertices.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The voltage-cancellation guarantee implies a bipartition, and the statement permits any safe subset of exactly k vertices.

common_affordance: The ability to obtain a larger safe set and arbitrarily discard vertices until exactly k remain

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It assumes that choosing the larger color class in each bipartite component gives a maximum independent set; mixed selections from both color classes can be larger, such as on a path.
It explicitly applies the incorrect shortcut that the voltage property means the answer is a larger color class, missing independent sets that mix both colors.
It uses the same larger-color-class construction, which is not generally a maximum independent set in a bipartite graph.

recommended_edit: Change the definition of an acceptable output to require an inclusion-wise maximal safe subset: in addition to having no internal links and exactly k vertices, every unselected component must be linked to at least one selected component.
